title: 美联储官员古尔斯比：通胀回落路径或难平稳
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: On the supply side, oil tariffs, commodity prices, et cetera, forecasters have spent more than a year now pushing back the date when inflation was
segments.zh: 在供给端，石油关税、大宗商品价格等，预测机构已经花了一年多时间推迟通胀见顶回落的预期时间。

segments.en: supposed to peak and start falling. So originally that was supposed to happen in the fourth quarter of 2025. Then Q1, 2026, then Q2, then Q3, then Q4, and now it's sometime in 2027.
segments.zh: 最初预计在2025年第四季度，然后推到2026年一季度、二季度、三季度、四季度，现在又到了2027年某个时候。

segments.en: That is not a comfortable pattern for identifying what is supposed to be a temporary inflation
segments.zh: 这种模式让人难以安心判断这是否只是暂时的通胀冲击。

segments.en: shock. Now, whether you attribute that to a steady stream of new supply shocks or you think the
segments.zh: 无论你将其归因于持续的新供给冲击，还是认为旧供给冲击比我们最初想的更持久，

segments.en: old supply shocks are just proving more persistent than we originally thought, this has definitely
segments.zh: 这显然不像一次性冲击的模式，而正如我所说，这种模式是忽略供给冲击的基础。

segments.en: not looked like the one and done pattern that as I said underpins the case for looking through the supply shock. So I want to see actual evidence that these shocks are fading or I find it
segments.zh: 所以我想看到这些冲击正在消退的实际证据，否则我很难看到一条可信的回到2%通胀的路径来证明继续忽略它们是合理的。

segments.en: hard to see a credible path back to 2% inflation that would justify continuing to look through them.
segments.zh: 很难看到一条可信的路径能让通胀回到2%，从而证明继续忽略这些压力是合理的。
